# Task 3 "Frame parser": third execution attempt

## Gate check before dispatch

- **Grant.** The spec header reads `**Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends`. The predicate finds one line, so the grant is active. Value decoding finds no fund token, so the grant gives amend permission and no funded rounds.
- **Hard stops.** None apply. The grant is well-formed, settings are available, there is no dirty-tree or commit-boundary return, and there is no `REJECT` and no redraw.
- **Takeable decision.** The latest `BLOCKED` names no repair, so I route nothing yet. I compare the failing parser assertion against task 3's transcript. It was not auto-resolved earlier on this task, so this is not the `evidence repeats` stop.
- **Execution escalation.** Two ordinary attempts have failed. `gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })` returned `implModel` `<resolved-model>`. This spends task 3's one execution escalation for this site, separately from review escalation and funding. Siblings stay as they are, with no fan-out and no re-chain. I make no `plan_tracker` write, so task 3 stays `in_progress`.

Announcement:

```
escalated round for task 3 after 2 failed attempts
```

Dispatch (D1). It uses the same payload and the same worktree isolation as the prior attempts, plus a fresh context:

```ts
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  model: "<resolved-model>",
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  worktree: true,
  tasks: [{
    agent: "implementer",
    outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
    task: `You are implementing Task 3: Frame parser
## Task Description
<FULL plan text of Task 3, verbatim>
## Context
Leg: <task Leg or home>; Rules: <combined spec/task Rules files - read before acting>
Spec: <abs spec path in /workspace/project>; Spec anchors: <Task 3 **Spec:** anchors>
Prior patch (start from it): <Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-<i>-implementer.patch
Work from: /workspace/project (isolated worktree from WAVE_BASE_SHA)
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <Task 3 Tests: command bullets, verbatim>
TEST_CONTRACT: <Task 3 **Tests:** block verbatim + Files: Create:/Test: paths>
Tests call the via: seam directly. Create every Create: path at exactly that path.
## Previous implementer report (BLOCKED), verbatim
<complete latest BLOCKED report, including the failing parser assertion output>
Report test-contract evidence per command and per via:; any unmet -> DONE_WITH_CONCERNS.
**Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT`
  }]
})
```

The returned patch supersedes the prior patch at integration.

## Result branches

**DONE.** This spends the escalation, and the ordinary gates still apply. I materialize the new patch with the snapshot block (`SR_ROOT='/workspace/project'`, `SR_BASE="$WAVE_BASE_SHA"`, `SR_PATCH=<new patch>`) and record its tree with the Fix-delta block. I then dispatch an initial `spec-reviewer` with `cwd` set to the snapshot. Its payload is the task text, the patch diff, the abs spec path, the anchors, the Tests block and the Test paths. It has no re-review marker. After saving the report, I run `git -C /workspace/project worktree remove --force <snapshot>`.

If SR returns `COMPLIANT`, I run `git -C /workspace/project apply --index <new patch>` and run each scoped command as `(cd /workspace/project && <cmd>)`. Then:
- I run `git -C /workspace/project add -A`.
- I dispatch one wave CR with `BASE_SHA: <WAVE_BASE_SHA>`, `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` and the wave's union of scoped commands.
- If CR returns `SHIP`, I run `git -C /workspace/project reset --soft "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" && git -C /workspace/project add -A && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "<wave msg>"`.
- Only then do I mark the wave's indices `complete`.

**BLOCKED recommending a named correction of the approved parser rule (no boundary change).** This row is a spec/plan rule edit taken under the grant, so I print `took recommendation: <parser-rule correction> for task 3`. Next I apply amendment-surface §5:
- I edit the spec and print `amended the spec: <title> - <what>`.
- I dispatch `plan-writer` with an `Amend:` block naming the parser section and an `In-flight:` list of the spec plus the parent's dirty paths.
- `plan_check` returns PASS. I read the plan once and update the tracker (task 3 stays `in_progress`; anchor-changed completed tasks reopen in place).
- I make one `git -C /workspace/project commit` of spec and plan. The subject is `amend: 1 item(s) - <title>`, the record is `granted`, and the body quotes `auto-apply amends`.

Task 3 then re-enters the task loop against the amended text. That re-entry is the amendment's named consequence, not a fourth unnamed repair, and the escalation stays spent.

**Dispatch error with Recommendation: none.** I emit the stop note below after the batch returns and end the turn. The header has no bracketed escalated clause because the dispatch errored. The phase stays `implement` and task 3 stays `in_progress`.

```
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task 3 (Frame parser).

Problem: the escalated dispatch failed: <quoted dispatch error>; two ordinary attempts had already ended BLOCKED on the parser assertion.

Fix options:
  a) <concrete parser change from the assertion>
  b) amend spec section <parser rule> so the frame boundary rule matches <evidence>

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: none - <why no named change is recommended>
```

**BLOCKED recommending more attempts.** This falls in the budget/consent row, so it is not takeable and gets no new dispatch. I emit a stop note whose header reads `Stopped on task 3 (Frame parser); escalated round on <resolved-model> did not resolve it.`. It quotes the `file:line` finding and the 1-3 line assertion snippet, and ends `Recommendation: more attempts - <why>`. Then I wait for the human.

## Resume scenes

**Task 3's exact escalation announcement exists.** The line `escalated round for task 3 after 2 failed attempts` in task 3's own transcript means the escalation is spent. I route whatever result was recovered through the branches above. If none was recovered, I emit a stop note with the latest evidence, with no re-dispatch and no fourth attempt.

**Only a sibling's announcement exists and task 3's history is missing.** Identity comes only from task 3's own exact line, and a sibling's line does not count. An unrecoverable identity means the escalation counts as spent, so I emit task 3's stop note, which ends in a `Recommendation:` line.

**Settings tool fails.** An unavailable `gauntlet_setting` is a configuration error. I stop and report the tool error, with no stop note, no dispatch and no manual settings merge.

**implModel is undefined.** I emit the existing stop note with no bracketed clause. Its `Problem:` line reads "no escalation model resolvable" and it skips the `file:line` and test lines. Task 3 stays `in_progress`.

**Header is budget-only** (e.g. `fund 3 fix rounds`). Budget-only gives no amend permission and authorizes no execution escalation, so the ordinary two-attempt stop holds. The stop note carries `budget: <spent> of 3 spent` after `Problem:`. If the funded-round lines cannot be recovered on resume, that line reads `budget: 3 of 3 spent (not recovered on resume)`.

**Explicit retry or a newly written grant.** Neither re-arms the execution escalation. A new grant funds review rounds or amends going forward only. I therefore route an explicit retry through the same stop and recommendation handling, never into a fourth unnamed implementer dispatch.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The supplied observations establish that task 3 is still `in_progress`; they are not execution results from me. In the payloads below, `<TASK>`, `<PATCH>`, `<REPORT>`, `<SPEC>`, `<PLAN>`, `<ANCHORS>`, `<TESTS>`, `<TEST_PATHS>`, `<COMMANDS>`, and `<BASE>` mean the existing full task text, absolute artifact/spec/plan paths, complete latest report, spec anchors, test contract, test paths, scoped commands, and recorded wave base—none of which were supplied literally.

### Third attempt

Print exactly `escalated round for task 3 after 2 failed attempts`, then dispatch the following single isolated implementer using the runtime-resolved model. This spends task 3’s one execution escalation; do not start a new chain, change tracker status, or consume review-funding credits.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  model: "<resolved-model>",
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  worktree: true,
  task: `
You are implementing Task 3: Frame parser.

## Existing task
<TASK>

## Existing isolated patch
<PATCH>
Read and apply this patch in your isolated worker checkout before repairing it.
Preserve existing task work and the original ownership/isolation boundaries.

## Complete latest implementer report
<REPORT>

## Context
Two ordinary implementation attempts failed. This is the single execution
escalation, not a review fix. Diagnose the reported parser assertion within
the approved task; do not silently change the approved parser rule.

Authoritative spec: <SPEC>
Spec anchors: <ANCHORS>
Leg and combined Rules: <existing values; read referenced files before acting>

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
<COMMANDS>

TEST_CONTRACT:
<TESTS>
Files Create/Test paths:
<TEST_PATHS>

Run the scoped commands and self-review. Report one met/unmet evidence line
per command and via seam; any unmet contract means DONE_WITH_CONCERNS.

Return explicitly:
**Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | NEEDS_CONTEXT | BLOCKED
DONE means implemented, scoped tests pass, and self-reviewed.
DONE_WITH_CONCERNS means implemented with deviations, risks, or unmet contract.
NEEDS_CONTEXT means required information is missing.
BLOCKED means the task cannot be completed.
Include implementation summary, evidence, remaining concerns, and any concrete
Recommendation. Do not write a parent report artifact yourself.
`
})
```

### Independent result: DONE

Retain accepted siblings and use the returned replacement patch—not the old patch—for a first spec review; materialize it from `<BASE>` with the following commands, retaining the snapshot until its terminal report is saved. Dispatch SR as shown, with no previous-review marker and no test execution; only accepted SR allows serial integration into `/workspace/project`, the scoped gate, and initial integrated-wave CR.

```bash
SR_ROOT='/workspace/project'
SR_BASE='<BASE>'
SR_PATCH='<returned absolute replacement patch path>'
SR_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
SR_TREE="$SR_DIR/tree"
git -C "$SR_ROOT" worktree add --detach "$SR_TREE" "$SR_BASE" || exit 1
git -C "$SR_TREE" apply --index "$SR_PATCH" || exit 1
printf 'snapshot: %s\n' "$SR_TREE"
```

```bash
FD_ROOT='<printed snapshot path>'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "<printed snapshot path>",
  output: "<absolute parent-selected SR report path>",
  task: `
Review Task 3: Frame parser.
<TASK>
Authoritative spec: <SPEC>
Spec anchors: <ANCHORS>
Leg and combined Rules: <existing values; read referenced files before acting>
Tests contract: <TESTS>
Test paths: <TEST_PATHS>
Patch: <returned replacement patch diff>
Implementer claims: <complete successful implementer report>

Start from diff hunks with file:line; read every touched file in full in this
snapshot. Read deleted files from <BASE>. Never execute tests.
Return Verdict: COMPLIANT, NEEDS_REWORK, or OUT_OF_SCOPE_CHANGES.
`
})
```

After saving and reading SR, remove its snapshot; conditional on compliance, integrate accepted patches serially, run every wave scoped command, and stage deliverables before the single initial wave CR. These are conditional next gates, not claimed verdicts; commit only after the actual required reviews accept.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project worktree remove --force '<printed snapshot path>'
# Only after COMPLIANT; apply every accepted wave patch serially:
git -C /workspace/project apply --index '<replacement patch path>'
# Repeat for each command in the wave's scoped-command union:
(cd /workspace/project && <scoped command verbatim>)
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# Capture the CR dispatch tree using the FD block above,
# substituting FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'.
```

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Use the supplied code-reviewer template.
DESCRIPTION: <integrated wave implementation summaries>
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <full wave tasks, Leg and combined Rules>
Read referenced rule files before reviewing.
BASE_SHA: <BASE>
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <wave command union>
Review the staged and unstaged integrated wave diff for production readiness.
`
})
```

```bash
# Only after all required gates accept:
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft '<BASE>' &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m 'Implement frame parser'
# Then mark the wave's existing indices complete, including task 3.
```

### Independent result: BLOCKED, named parser-rule correction

Classify the evidence-backed correction as an amendment, not another implementation decision: re-read `<SPEC>`’s header, validate the active amend grant, and read amendment-surface section 5 before applying the recommended old-to-new rule text, printing `amended the spec: Parser rule - <what changes>`. Dispatch `plan-writer` in `/workspace/project` with `Amend: <corrected section and quoted assertion evidence>`, `In-flight: <actual parent workflow paths, including spec>`, and “preserve every task title and wave position the amendment does not touch; edit only affected anchors and tasks,” then run parent `plan_check` and read the amended plan after the stipulated PASS. Commit spec and plan together as one `amend:` commit containing the `granted` audit record, quoted grant, and evidence; keep task 3 `in_progress`, and do not dispatch a fourth unnamed repair or reset its spent execution escalation.

### Independent result: dispatch error, `Recommendation: none`

Stop with a note beginning `gauntlet: question` and `Stopped on task 3 (Frame parser).`, stating the actual dispatch error in `Problem:` without claiming that an escalated round ran successfully. Offer concrete parser-rule correction or a separate prerequisite change only if supported by the report, and end `Recommendation: none - the dispatch failed and no supported correction was identified`; retain the prior isolated patch and `in_progress` status.

### Independent result: BLOCKED, recommends more attempts

Stop with the escalated-round clause naming `<resolved-model>` and quote the actual BLOCKED reason; “more attempts” is consent, not an actionable in-task repair. End `Recommendation: none - additional attempts do not authorize another execution escalation`, preserving the patch and task status.

### Resume: exact task announcement exists

Recover task 3’s execution escalation as spent from `escalated round for task 3 after 2 failed attempts`; recover its actual result and continue only the corresponding branch above. An explicit retry or newly written grant does not re-arm execution escalation.

### Resume: sibling announcement only, task history missing

Do not attribute the sibling’s escalation to task 3, but treat task 3’s unrecoverable execution-escalation history as spent. Stop on its unresolved BLOCKED return rather than dispatching another escalated implementer.

### Resume: settings tool fails

Report the unavailable `gauntlet_setting` tool as a configuration error and stop before dispatch. Do not substitute a model, reconstruct settings through shell commands, or emit the escalation announcement.

### Resume: `implModel` undefined

Stop before dispatch with `Problem: no escalation model resolvable` and no escalated-round header clause. Keep task 3 `in_progress`; amend permission cannot supply a missing model.

### Resume: header is budget-only

A budget-only header grants no amendment permission and no implementer-failure execution escalation after the two ordinary failures. Stop under the ordinary failure rule; review-funding credits remain unused and cannot buy a third implementation attempt.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and moves the two Before missed. On dispatch, Before explicitly declined the fixed wording and printed `escalated round for task 3 (Frame parser) on <resolved-model>`; After prints the exact `escalated round for task 3 after 2 failed attempts` line, resolves implModel first, and makes one fresh synchronous resolved-model dispatch with the same isolation, prior patch, complete BLOCKED report and SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS while stating it is separate from review funding. On hard-stops, Before let the escalation proceed under a budget-only header ("the escalation still proceeds on <resolved-model>"), contradicting the fact; After states budget-only authorizes no execution escalation and the ordinary two-attempt stop holds. Outcome and recovery were already satisfied in Before and remain so, with After additionally ending every stop note in a `Recommendation:` line and keeping the amendment re-entry named rather than a fourth unnamed repair. To keep this in future wording, retain the literal announcement string as a fixed token, keep the budget-only scene phrased as a stop before any escalated dispatch (not as a funding/escalation independence note), and keep the sibling-line and retry/new-grant scenes explicitly resolving to "spent, no dispatch".

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moved `dispatch` to holds by printing the exact `escalated round for task 3 after 2 failed attempts` line, tying the dispatch to the runtime-resolved model, carrying the complete report, patch, anchors, scoped commands and worktree isolation, and stating that review-funding credits are not consumed; Before used a different announcement sentence and never showed the escalationLoop.implModel resolution step, so a careful reader could not confirm the required header. Before already satisfied `outcome` (DONE → SR/integration/tests/CR, named correction → granted amendment with plan-writer and amend commit, error/none and more-attempts → stop), `recovery` (exact-announcement recovery, retry/grant never re-arm, sibling-only/missing history never redispatches) and `hard-stops`, and After keeps all three. One wording tightening would make After even safer on `dispatch`: state explicitly that the model comes from `gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" }).implModel` in the third-attempt section itself rather than only implying it through the resume scenes, so the resolution and the announcement both appear before the payload.
